= Module 4: Export the Llama Stack Client Code and Clean Up
:navtitle: 4. View Code & Clean Up

⏱ *Estimated time: 3 minutes*

== Learning objectives

By the end of this module you will be able to:

* Find the auto-generated Python Llama Stack client script in the Playground UI
* Identify the four key elements of the script: import, client instantiation, model name, and `responses.create()` call
* Delete the Playground and confirm the empty state

== Exercise 1: Open the View Code modal

. In the Playground toolbar (top-right), click *View Code*.
+
A *Playground configuration* modal opens. The header shows *PYTHON* — indicating the
generated code is a Python script.

. The script is a *Llama Stack Quickstart Script* that replicates the current
  Playground configuration programmatically.

=== Verify

✔ The modal is open and shows numbered lines of Python code.

image::13-view-code-modal.png[Playground configuration modal showing Llama Stack Python quickstart script labeled PYTHON,link=self,window=blank,width=700]

== Exercise 2: Read the generated code

Study the four key sections of the script:

[source,python]
----
from llama_stack_client import LlamaStackClient  # <1>

client = LlamaStackClient(base_url=LLAMA_STACK_URL)  # <2>

model_name = "maas-vllm-inference-1/qwen38-27b"  # <3>
system_instructions = """You are a helpful AI assistant..."""

config = {
    "input": input_text,
    "model": model_name,
    "instructions": system_instructions
}
response = client.responses.create(**config)  # <4>
print("agent>", response.output_text)
----
<1> *Import* — the `llama_stack_client` Python package provides the SDK
<2> *Client instantiation* — `LlamaStackClient` connects to the Llama Stack server URL
<3> *Model name* — matches the model you selected in Module 2 (`{model_name}`)
<4> *Create call* — `client.responses.create()` is the programmatic equivalent of clicking Send in the chat UI

. Confirm that `model_name` in the script matches your selected model: `{model_name}`.

. Notice `LLAMA_STACK_URL = ""` — this placeholder would be set to the cluster endpoint
  to run the script outside the browser.
+
NOTE: Running this script is out of scope for this lab. The key takeaway is that
every chat interaction you did in the UI has a direct Python API equivalent.

=== Verify

✔ You can identify all four callout elements in the script (import, client, model_name, responses.create).

image::15-delete-dialog-confirmed.png[Delete playground dialog with User Mhepburn Project typed to confirm — Delete button active,link=self,window=blank,width=700]

== Exercise 3: Close the modal and delete the Playground

. Click the *✕* to close the View Code modal.

. In the Playground toolbar, click the three-dot overflow menu *⋮*.

. Click *Delete playground*.

. A confirmation dialog appears: *"Delete playground?"*
+
IMPORTANT: This action cannot be undone and deletes the Playground for *all users*
in this project.

. In the text field, type the exact project name to confirm:
+
[source,text,role="execute",subs="attributes"]
----
{learner_project}
----
+
TIP: The *Delete* button remains grayed out until you type the exact project name.
If the button does not become red/active, check your spelling.

. Click *Delete*.

=== Verify

✔ The Playground returns to the *"Create your playground"* empty state. The Playground
and its chat history have been removed.

image::16-playground-empty-after-delete.png[Playground empty state after deletion — Create your playground CTA returned,link=self,window=blank,width=700]
